answer: Radio proves where a seat sits. Each seat owns a low-power transmitter bound to one map cell, and each epoch the seed names three; the seat reports signal strength and arrival time for each. Five witnesses from distinct cells must agree, and two seats in one cell count once, costing the pair 120,000 POA apiece. A position turns credible only when the cells around it echo it back. A thousand shadow seats need a thousand transmitters heard by living neighbours: $180,000 of hardware plus installs, on ground as bare as a tundra. A mirror reflects an orchard without bearing a single apple.
